conventions.convention: Full AC is assumed. Brownian increments must be independent of the filtration at the left endpoint; adaptedness alone is insufficient. Vector stochastic integrals are coordinatewise scalar Itô integrals.

The initial law is a Borel probability supported in the closed Euclidean ball of finite radius R≥0. The scalar coefficient g is C1, positive and bounded away from zero; v(t)=∫₀ᵗg(r)²dr. The initial law need not have a density.

Weak forward solutions are narrowly continuous probability curves satisfying the displayed identity for C1-in-time, C2-in-space tests on [0,T] with a common compact spatial support; their initial measure is μ.

W2 is the square root of the infimum of quadratic costs over Borel probability couplings of finite-second-moment laws. The endpoint estimate concerns truncation alone and makes no density or score assertion at zero.
The score is ∇log p_t. Jacobian norms are Euclidean operator norms. Uniform Lipschitz and growth bounds hold on [ε,T] with 0<ε<T, without a uniform bound as ε decreases to zero.

load_bearing.statement: Under Full AC, compactly supported Borel initial law and the stated usual filtered Brownian setup, p_t(x)=∫φ_v(t)(x−z)μ(dz) is a finite, strictly positive normalized law density for t>0. The transition density is q(s,x;t,y)=φ_(v(t)−v(s))(y−x), satisfies the displayed joint-law identity for Borel sets, and obeys Chapman–Kolmogorov. No initial density is assumed.

Under its Full AC, complete filtered Brownian and deterministic C1 positive bounded integrand hypotheses, M_t−M_s is independent of F_s and has law N_d(0,(v(t)−v(s))I_d) for every 0≤s<t≤T. Consequently its increments over every finite increasing time list are mutually independent.

Under the stated Full AC and compact-support Gaussian smoothing hypotheses, p_t is positive and infinitely differentiable in space for t>0, is continuously differentiable in time on [ε,T], and satisfies ∂_t p_t=(g(t)²/2)Δp_t. Its probability curve, with initial measure μ, is the unique narrowly continuous weak forward solution in the stated test class.

For the stated compact-support Gaussian convolution under Full AC, on [ε,T] the posterior mean m and covariance C give s_t(x)=−(x−m)/v(t) and D_xs_t(x)=−I_d/v(t)+C/v(t)². The operator norm is at most 1/v(ε)+R²/v(ε)² and |s_t(x)|≤(|x|+R)/v(ε), yielding the stated uniform global Lipschitz bound.

Under the stated Full AC and compact-support Gaussian smoothing hypotheses, for every 0<ε≤T, E|X_ε−X_0|²=dv(ε) and W2(μ_ε,μ)≤√(dv(ε)). As ε decreases to zero, X_ε converges in probability to X_0 and μ_ε converges weakly to μ. This controls endpoint truncation only and asserts no density or score regularity at zero.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 calls ψ_L(s,x)=χ_L(x)h(s,x) an admissible test, but step 1.3 defines h only for 0≤s≤t, whereas the Statement requires admissible tests on [0,T]. For t<T an extension past t is unstated. A C1-in-time, C2-in-space extension exists using the smooth terminal data, so this is a small justification gap rather than a false uniqueness claim.
